3924ceb24d7bb216652f218076612de4771cee05.content: Replacing an embedding generation invalidates the target provider/model active grounding calibration, even when the new index has the same node count. Grounding calibration staleness based only on row count cannot detect changed dimensions or a recomputed generation. Delete only the exact active target calibration key in the same transaction as vector reset. Keep calibration history, other model records and unrelated metadata, and retain the old active record in the recovery backup. A failed target-table creation must roll back both the vector reset and active-calibration invalidation. Implementation: src/kindex/embedding_rebuild.py; calibration loading: src/kindex/grounding.py. This is derived-state invalidation tied to explicit index replacement.

53ce8de265ce189595779e59edfd3491ef60efdd.content: kindex-lite --repo binds an MCP endpoint to the canonical local .kin graph and Kinbase sync/status/explain/submit operations for that repository. src/kindex/mcp_lite.py owns an explicit tool allowlist and per-call path validation. src/kindex/mcp_server.py accepts request-local dependencies without replacing the full server singleton. Ambient profile, config, graph routing, vector providers, executable reminders, and host ingestion are excluded. This is an MCP capability boundary, not an OS sandbox. A fresh graph initializes locally; tracked snapshots are not automatically imported and old schema migration requires explicit preparation. See docs/mcp-lite.md. Local implementation; release and live Factory configuration are separate. Explicit outbound submissions use content-addressed single-observation SQLite artifacts with agent provenance and team audience. Native Kinbase ingestion owns derivation/admission and can admit local facts; no separate bulk corpus admission or authority ratification is requested. Actual native signed-fixture verification confirmed ai_generated provenance and idempotent unchanged retry. Existing ordinary config tests require an isolated HOME to avoid ambient profile and host session fixture contamination.

85d06bc4eebd83f52ef953e74c1eb3f15b9460ce.content: CLI --json output must remain one parseable JSON document even when --verbose is requested. The embedding rebuild command disables per-node stdout progress in JSON mode; preview and backup diagnostics stay on stderr. An operation that succeeds but emits invalid JSON still fails its automation contract. Keep normal verbose progress for human-readable output. This is the existing wire-format boundary failure pattern, not a new taxonomy category. Regression: tests/test_embedding_rebuild.py::test_json_verbose_rebuild_keeps_stdout_machine_readable. Implementation: src/kindex/cli.py, cmd_embed rebuild branch.

b8da96fba34301f6553c66c0dbc2cbf07959252d.content: kindex-lite --repo binds memory to one repository without ambient graph or profile fallback. It uses an explicit allowlist and validates local storage each call. Kinbase defaults to sync/explain reads; --allow-kinbase-submit enables explicit agent-evidence submissions and native status, which may write overdue apology events. --no-kinbase removes all Kinbase tools. Permissions are fixed by the launcher, not tool arguments. Saved source locators outside the selected database remain unresolved. Local memory remains writable in every mode. This is an MCP capability boundary, not an OS sandbox: shell, hooks, and other servers need separate host controls. Tracked knowledge.json or knowledge.jsonl is not automatically imported. Existing schemas requiring migration need explicit preparation. Native submissions preserve Kinbase derivation/admission receipts, not authority ratification. See docs/mcp-lite.md for configuration and evidence limits.

provenance.prov_why: User requested per-agent Kinbase write control; source integration with current main
